Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.

ABSENT:  Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi and Council Member McGowan

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Kallman, City Attorney Rusin, City Clerk Cook,
  Community Development Director Brady, Acting Public Works
  Director Wieske, and Chief Hellinga

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION: Moved by Council Member Kemps and Seconded by Council Member Roos
to approve the agenda.

AYES:  Murdock, Roos, Kemps,
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  McGowan, Lozzi

MAYOR’S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Mayor Murdock thanked the PVE Foundation and residents for their donation of
$466,210 for ALPR cameras that were approved on the September 10, 2024 consent
agenda. She reminded residents that Saturday, September 24 is bulky trash pick up
and that the PVE Tree Lighting event will be Sunday, December 1 from 5-7 P.M. and
the Santa Parade will be Sunday, December 15. The Mayor reminded PVE seniors of
the upcoming Bohannon lecture series at the Peninsula Seniors.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR & CLOSED SESSION MEETINGS SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 In her “Did You Know” segment, the Mayor discussed the City’s history of relying on
special taxes to fund capital improvement projects. She discussed the 1983 10% utility
tax that ran a total of 20 years until 2002 and provided almost as much revenue as the
parcel tax that was in place at the time. It was replaced in 2003 with a special sewer tax
that ran from 2003-2013. There have been no dedicated revenue sources for capital
projects for the past 10 years, though funds from prior year operating surpluses have
been set aside.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Kallman reported ongoing issues with the city’s Granicus system which is
affecting our ability to livestream and post recordings of public meetings. While this is
resolved, tonight’s council meeting was being recorded and available on Zoom.

Chief Hellinga provided tips on how to make one’s house unattractive to burglars and
announced the department is selling pink patches for Breast Cancer Awareness.
Proceeds from this fundraiser that is being run by the POA and not city resources will go
to a detective in Inglewood that is battling breast cancer.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Council was addressed by John Credell and Gerry Brooke.

   GRANTS PASS SUPREME COURT RULING

  Council was addressed by a representative from the SBCCOG.

  Council members discussed the pledge and concerns with some of the elements
  and elected to not proceed with it.

  There was no public comment.

NEW BUSINESS

12. MALAGA LANE WATER INTRUSION AND SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION

  City Manager Kallman introduced the Interim Public Works Director Derek Wieske
  who provided an update on issues with water intrusion in Malaga Cove and the sink
  hole. He reported that Staff is soliciting bids to fill the sink hole and other voids
  identified by the ground penetrating radar scan. Additionally, Staff is looking at
  other medium term solutions for reducing the water table. Council provided
  direction that this matter be a standing agenda item.

  Council was addressed by Tom Schmidt.

13. CITY COUNCIL DISCUSSION ON CONSIDERATION OF MOVING FORWARD
  ON PAID PARKING CONCEPTS

  There was no public comment.

  City Manager Kallman provided a staff report and asked for Council direction.
  Council provided direction to proceed with securing a vendor to conduct a paid
  parking study and that the scope of the study should include
  o Recommendation on where, if any, to implement paid parking (e.g., Malaga
  Cove Plaza, RAT beach area, Lunada Bay Plaza, street parking along the
  coast)
  o Potential revenue
  o If time limits for any spots need to be adjusted (longer or shorter)
  o Required capabilities
  o Any changes to parking configuration
  o Timing of parking slots
  o Implementation and ongoing costs
  o Identification of potential unintended consequences and suggested
  mitigation approaches

MAYOR AND COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS

TENTATIVE FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

REGULAR & CLOSED SESSION MEETINGS SEPTEMBER 24, 2024
 Mayor Murdock asked for a future item for adjusting the In Lieu of Payment for tree
removal to ensure the fee covers planting costs. She also reminded Staff of the long
overdue fee schedule study/update.

There was no public comment related to the Closed Session.
